title: Dynamic model-sourcing heatmap and procurement trigger playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Build a continuously-updating, risk-weighted heatmap that ranks model vendors and on-prem/private variants across latency, regional availability, quantization compatibility, price delta, SLA risk, and observed quality drift. Deliver a decision playbook that maps heatmap thresholds to procurement actions (reserve capacity, trigger canary rollouts, negotiate price floors, or flip to fallback model family).

Key deliverables:
- Looker/Console heatmap dashboard with configurable time windows and signal weighting (link in comments).
- Confluence playbook (procurement-trigger runbook) with decision tree, stakeholder contact matrix, and template contract clauses to accelerate negotiation for high-risk vendors.
- Signal ingestion spec (sources: runtime telemetry, provider availability API, model-compatibility testbed results, market price feeds).
- Simulated scenario workbook (failure and detect->fallback timelines) and automated alert rules that surface to #model-sourcing and PagerDuty.

Acceptance criteria:
- Dashboard refresh latency <= 5 minutes for primary signals and exposes an API endpoint for programmatic queries.
- At least 6 signal types ingested and normalized (latency, error-rate, capacity, cost-per-token, quant-compat score, eval drift metric).
- Playbook reviewed and signed off by Legal and Security for contract/NDAs clauses.
- Automation demonstrates a simulated failover from primary to fallback family within the dashboard and records expected token-cost delta.

Success metrics (first 6 months):
- Reduce customer incidents caused by model supply shocks by 40%.
- Decrease median time-to-failover from detection to fallback from current baseline by 60%.
- Cut procurement decision cycle for emergency capacity by 30%.

Risks & mitigations:
- Signal freshness: prioritize telemetry channels and provide conservative move-to-fallback thresholds.
- Vendor NDA constraints on telemetry: identify fallbacks that don’t rely on proprietary signals and negotiate minimal telemetry sharing.
- Noise/false positives: require multi-signal confirmation before automated procurement actions; initial rollout is advisory-only.

Next steps (this cycle):
1) Wire up telemetry connectors (Eng) and validate 3 core signals (latency, error-rate, capacity).
2) Produce initial heatmap prototype and run tabletop simulation.
3) Legal/security review of playbook language and procurement automation.
4) Stakeholder review and pilot with one enterprise account for runbook validation.
